title: Smooth separated finitely presented maps with integral geometric fibres
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $T$ an $S$-scheme, and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Regard $T$ as its represented space and use the canonical Yoneda maps and sheaf fibre products [def-sfb-smooth-integral-group-space]. For a morphism $p:X\to h_T$, define the smooth integral fibre condition by the existing chart tests [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]: $p$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], separated, locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and both $p$ and its relative diagonal are quasi-compact. For every algebraically closed field $K$ in the scheme universe and $s:\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$, require the point space of $X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}K$ to be irreducible (hence nonempty) and every representable etale scheme chart of this fibre to be reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. This is nonempty geometric integrality, in the same convention as the structural case. No group law or section is part of the definition. For every morphism $a:T\prime\to T$ of $S$-schemes, the base changed map is the actual second projection $X\times_T T\prime\to h_{T\prime}$ of that sheaf fibre product.
